correctness.rationale: A pure two-named-equivalence structure has exactly four possible existential witness bits a,b,c,d at rank one (with x itself always available but not a distinct witness). Occupied E×F cells form a simple bipartite support weighted by intersection multiplicity; a indicates multiplicity≥2, b/c degree≥2 on each side, d existence of an occupied nonincident cell. If some d=0 the support lies in two incident stars with at most five bit types; otherwise all types d=1 and the remaining 3 bits allow at most eight. Eight types require four weight1 and four weight2 cells, hence |X|≥12, and the displayed 12-point partitions realize them. At equality each type names a unique cell, with two isolated cells and two (1,1) core cells. Disjoint, shared-left, shared-right core incidences each have four leaf-weight choices. An independent support-incidence enumeration recovered 12 possible edge-equality support templates. The original 324,446,969-instance C++ n=12 log is supporting provenance, not rerun; the structural classification, not a timeout or log, proves all-N bound and 12 isomorphism types. A rank-two sentence has outer quantified variable applied to a pointed rank-one property, so extremizers sharing all eight types agree on rank-two sentences.
residual_risks: The exact template count is for equality in 12-element structures with two NAMED equivalences; interchanging E and F changes isomorphism type.
The huge C++ verification was inspected as code and stored output, not rerun; an independent small support-template enumeration checked the 12 combinatorial configurations.
